review_type: Independent Tiny request-retention implementation source review
source_reasoning: retainRequest acquisition and requestRetired decision are serialized under the same private state monitor; an accepted hold wins before retirement or receives terminal no-op afterward.

The worker waits for nonaborted finished-request holds. Last-release notification only acquires short state monitor, with no transport IO/response monitor, and wakeup condition is rechecked under state.
After acquiring the IO monitor the worker rechecks setup/retention under state before requestRetired=true. A late hold acquired while worker waits for IO cannot be lost.
RequestRetentions releases its helper monitor before invoking its notify observer; state-to-helper acquisition/count queries therefore have no helper-to-state lock inversion.

Abort atomically refuses repeated/retired calls, permits forced termination of finished-but-retained requests, marks aborted before unlocking and notifies listeners/drain outside both monitors. Worker ignores revoked holds only for aborted requests. Late retains are no-op and late releases only notify.

Request hold release neither finishes a pending response nor overrides independent settingUpStream/running-drain ownership. Existing setup wait and once drain cancellation remain intact; physical worker return still follows IO-owner exit.
Ordinary finish does not invoke abort listeners. Full successful cleanup releases the hold then permits normal retirement; no mutation to first IO failure/cause classification or input bytes.
